prompt: Match each idle resource to the property that gives it away.
Why does the lesson run Resource Graph's query in the emulator instead of against Resource Graph?

choices.text: Resource Graph does not understand KQL
choices.why: It answers in KQL; that is why the query carries over.

choices.text: Resource Graph needs a signed-in identity
choices.why: Right. The same query, run against a table of the same shape.

choices.text: The emulator returns more accurate results
choices.why: It returns what the generated table holds, nothing more.

choices.text: Resource Graph is billed per query
choices.why: Cost is not the reason given.

prompt: Three of the four idle resources have an empty owner. Why does that matter more than their cost?
hint: Who will be asked about them?

choices.text: Untagged resources are billed at a higher rate
choices.why: Tags do not change prices.

choices.text: Azure deletes untagged resources after 30 days
choices.why: Nothing deletes resources for lack of tags.

choices.text: Resource Graph cannot see untagged resources
choices.why: It found them; tags are just a column.

choices.text: Nobody is asked to keep or delete them
choices.why: Right. Lesson 24 is about that.

prompt: Why does rightsize.kql judge a VM by its 95th percentile rather than its average CPU?
hint: Where does an undersized VM fall over?

choices.text: A VM sized to the average falls over at the peak
choices.why: Right. The busiest hours have to fit.

choices.text: Advisor only accepts percentiles
choices.why: Advisor's rule is a threshold; the reason is the peak.

choices.text: The average is always higher than the 95th percentile
choices.why: It is lower, which is the problem.

choices.text: Perf rows have no averages
choices.why: The query computes both.

prompt: The projection doubles the 95th percentile for half the vCPUs. What does it leave out?
hint: CPU is one resource of several.

choices.text: Nothing; CPU scales exactly with vCPUs
choices.why: Roughly, and only CPU.

choices.text: Memory, disk and network
choices.why: Right. A smaller size also has less of those.

choices.text: The VM's operating system licence
choices.why: Licences do not change load; resources do.

choices.text: The hours between 1 and 4
choices.why: Every hour is in the percentile.

prompt: The Log Analytics table that holds performance counters such as `% Processor Time` is called ___.
Why does the shop still write its own rightsizing query when Advisor gives recommendations for free?

choices.text: Advisor recommendations are often wrong
choices.why: The lesson does not say so; it says a query can be read and extended.

choices.text: Advisor does not cover virtual machines
choices.why: It does; rightsizing VMs is one of its rules.

choices.text: A query shows its reasoning and can add tags
choices.why: Right. Advisor is where to start; a query is how to argue.

choices.text: Advisor needs Defender for Cloud
choices.why: It is free and independent.

prompt: vm-reports never passed 2% CPU in two weeks. What does the lesson conclude?
hint: What do those two weeks not contain?

choices.text: Delete it today
choices.why: It runs the month-end reports, outside the window.

choices.text: Schedule it to run at month end
choices.why: Right. Idle 28 days, essential 2.

choices.text: Double its size for safety
choices.why: Nothing in the data asks for more.

choices.text: Leave it exactly as it is
choices.why: It costs money for 28 idle days a month.

prompt: Put the shop's steps for acting on a rightsizing finding in order.
items: Check the workload's calendar with them
Make the reversible change through the pipeline
Record the saving from the cost export
trap: Changing before finding the owner is the slip: Thursday's incident was a resize nobody else knew about.

prompt: Which action is reversible for an unattached disk nobody claims?

choices.text: Delete it at once
choices.why: That cannot be undone.

choices.text: Move it to another subscription
choices.why: That moves the cost, not the problem.

choices.text: Leave it, since disks are cheap
choices.why: Premium disks are not, and it serves nothing.

choices.text: Snapshot it, then delete
choices.why: Right. A snapshot costs less and brings it back if needed.

prompt: Which of these did the lesson run? Choose all that apply.
hint: Queries over generated tables, yes; Azure services, no.

choices.text: The idle-resource query, over a Resources-shaped table
choices.why: Yes. In the emulator.

choices.text: The 95th percentile of CPU per VM
choices.why: Yes. rightsize.kql.

choices.text: az graph query against the subscription
choices.why: No. It needs a signed-in identity.

choices.text: Advisor's cost recommendations
choices.why: No. Advisor lives in a subscription.
